encounters.cc: Intermittent bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss over 6 months with up to six daily bowel movements and nocturnal stools

lines: Intermittent bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss over 6 months with up to six daily bowel movements and nocturnal stools
A 23-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of intermittent bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss.
She reports having up to six bowel movements daily, often with nocturnal stools.
- Crohn disease (diagnosed age 22; initially classified as ulcerative colitis)
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
She denies any family history of gastrointestinal diseases.
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).
On physical examination, she has mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Stool cultures and Clostridium difficile toxin assays are negative.
Colonoscopy shows continuous mucosal inflammation and ulceration starting from the rectum and extending proximally to the splenic flexure.
There are also several areas of swollen mucosa that appear as pseudopolyps.
Biopsies from the affected areas show chronic inflammation limited to the mucosa and submucosa.

encounters.cc: Fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, and frequent dizziness for the past two months

lines: Fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, and frequent dizziness for the past two months
She returns with fatigue, dyspnea, dizziness with ulcerative colitis history.
She has been following a strict vegan diet for the past year and does not take any supplements.
- Crohn disease (diagnosed age 22; initially classified as ulcerative colitis)
She denies any other medical history.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).
On physical examination, her skin appears pale, and her conjunctivae are pale as well.
Cardiovascular examination reveals a systolic murmur.

encounters.cc: Intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and progressive weight loss over 6 months with up to six loose stools daily, occasionally bloody

lines: Intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and progressive weight loss over 6 months with up to six loose stools daily, occasionally bloody
The patient returns to the gastroenterology clinic following prior encounters in January 2020 and July 2020, with established Crohn disease and iron deficiency anemia.
She presents with a 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss.
She reports that her symptoms have progressively worsened over the last two months.
She has experienced up to six loose stools per day, occasionally with blood.
- Crohn disease (diagnosed age 22; initially classified as ulcerative colitis)
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
She denies any family history of gastrointestinal diseases.
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).
On physical examination, she is afebrile, and her abdominal exam reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant without rebound or guarding.
A perianal examination shows a draining fistula.
Colonoscopy shows discontinuous areas of inflamed mucosa with intervening segments of normal-appearing bowel,

encounters.cc: Painful red bumps on her shins for 2 weeks, appeared suddenly and increased in number

lines: Painful red bumps on her shins for 2 weeks, appeared suddenly and increased in number
The patient is a 29-year-old female with Crohn disease and iron deficiency anemia who presents with a 2-week history of painful red bumps on her shins.
She reports that the bumps appeared suddenly and have increased in number.
She denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or new sexual partners.
Her past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis, which is currently well-controlled on mesalamine.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, there are multiple 2- to 3-cm tender, erythematous nodules on the anterior aspects of both lower legs.
There is no joint swelling or abdominal tenderness.
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR): 40 mm/hr (normal range: 0-20 mm/hr)

encounters.cc: Painful red bumps on legs for 3 weeks accompanied by 2-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and 5 kg unintentional weight loss

lines: Painful red bumps on legs for 3 weeks accompanied by 2-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and 5 kg unintentional weight loss
The patient with Crohn disease presents with recurrent bumps on her legs and gastrointestinal symptoms.
She reports that the bumps appeared suddenly and have increased in number.
She also mentions a 2-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss of 5 kg.
Her past medical history is significant for iron deficiency anemia.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).
On physical examination, there are multiple tender, erythematous nodules measuring 2-3 cm on her anterior shins.
Her abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Stool cultures and Clostridium difficile toxin assay are negative.

encounters.cc: Painful, deep nodules on lower legs for 6 weeks accompanied by low-grade fevers, joint aches, and occasional fatigue

lines: Painful, deep nodules on lower legs for 6 weeks accompanied by low-grade fevers, joint aches, and occasional fatigue

The patient is a 30-year-old female with Crohn disease and prior erythema nodosum episodes in 2022 who returns with painful deep nodules on her lower legs accompanied by low-grade fevers, joint aches, and occasional fatigue.
She states the nodules appeared suddenly and are tender to the touch, sometimes making it uncomfortable to wear jeans or walk long distances.
She denies recent insect bites, medication changes, or new skincare products, but reports a sore throat with cough approximately one month ago that resolved without treatment.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).
Physical examination reveals multiple poorly demarcated, warm, erythematous plaques and subcutaneous nodules along the anterior shins; some are beginning to fade with a yellowish hue.
No mucosal involvement or active joint swelling is noted.
A rapid streptococcal antigen test is now negative.

encounters.cc: Worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days with greenish vomitus and obstipation

lines: Worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days with greenish vomitus and obstipation
The patient is a 31-year-old female with Crohn disease initially classified as ulcerative colitis at age 22 who presents with a 2-day history of worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
She notes greenish vomitus and has not passed flatus or had a bowel movement since the symptoms started.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
She mentions that she has been smoking a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 10 years
She has a low-grade fever of 37.8°C (100°F)
On examination, her abdomen is distended and tender to palpation, with hyperactive bowel sounds
Laboratory tests reveal a white blood cell count of 12,000/uL, hemoglobin of 13.2 g/dL, and a C-reactive protein of 25 mg/L
An abdominal X-ray shows dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels

encounters.cc: Follow-up visit to assess disease control after previous flares and hospitalization

lines: Follow-up visit to assess disease control after previous flares and hospitalization
The patient returns for follow-up of her Crohn disease following recent hospitalization.

She previously experienced frequent flares requiring corticosteroids and biologic therapy but reports significant clinical improvement over the past year, with normalization of bowel movements and no abdominal pain.
- Small bowel obstruction due to fibrotic stricture secondary to Crohn's disease (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 6 months ago; previously 1 pack per day for 10 years).

Biopsy reveals decreased lamina propria lymphocyte infiltration and increased expression of a cytokine secreted by regulatory T cells that inhibits the synthesis of IFN-γ and TNF-α by effector T cells.
Colonoscopy now shows reduced mucosal inflammation compared to prior studies.
This cytokine is thought to contribute to sustained mucosal healing and long-term remission in inflammatory bowel disease.
